record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Prove that the scaling limit of true self-avoiding walk in dimensions greater than 2 is Brownian motion.

evidence.quote: Prove that the scaling limit of True Self Avoiding Walk in d > 2 is Brownian Motion.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 3$. The "true" (or myopic) self-avoiding walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is the nearest-neighbor, non-Markovian random walk $(X_n)_{n \geq 0}$ defined as follows. For each site $x \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and time $n$, let
$$\ell_n(x) = \#\{0 \leq k \leq n : X_k = x\}$$
denote the local time of the walk at $x$ up to time $n$. Fix a parameter $\beta > 0$. Conditionally on the past $(X_0, X_1, \dots, X_n)$, the walker jumps from $X_n$ to a nearest neighbor $y$ of $X_n$ with probability proportional to $\exp(-\beta \, \ell_n(y))$; that is,
$$\mathbb{P}\bigl(X_{n+1} = y \mid X_0,\dots,X_n\bigr) = \frac{e^{-\beta \ell_n(y)}}{\sum_{z \sim X_n} e^{-\beta \ell_n(z)}}, \qquad y \sim X_n.$$
Thus the walk is pushed toward neighbors visited less often in the past. Take $X_0 = 0$.

Prove that for every $d > 2$, the diffusively rescaled process
$$\Bigl( \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{N}}\, X_{\lfloor N t \rfloor} \Bigr)_{t \geq 0}$$
converges in distribution, as $N \to \infty$, to a non-degenerate Brownian motion on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (with some non-trivial isotropic covariance matrix $\sigma^2 I_d$).
artifact.status_search_result: Horváth, Tóth and Vető (Probab. Theory Related Fields, 2012) established a diffusive (Brownian) scaling limit for the "true"/myopic self-avoiding walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \geq 3$, but only in a stationary and ergodic regime obtained via a suitable initial condition (and, for the discrete model, under a weak-coupling condition). A full invariance principle starting from a fixed point $X_0 = 0$ in all $d \geq 3$ at arbitrary coupling has not been established in full generality, so the problem is generally regarded as partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Diffusive limits for "true" (or myopic) self-avoiding random walks and self-repellent Brownian polymers in d ≥ 3
status_evidence.snippet: In three and more dimensions, in a stationary (and ergodic) regime, the displacement of the moving particle scales diffusively.
status_evidence.claim: Diffusive scaling limit proved in a stationary regime for d ≥ 3 by Horváth–Tóth–Vető.

status_evidence.title: Diffusive limits for true self-avoiding random walks in d ≥ 3 (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: Diffusive limits for 'true' (or myopic) self-avoiding random walks and self-repellent Brownian polymers in d ≥ 3.
status_evidence.claim: Published version confirming partial resolution of the conjecture in stationary regime.
